newsitem.title: USA: Senate Republicans urged to approve Labor nominee.
newsitem.headline: Senate Republicans urged to approve Labor nominee.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle urged majority Republicans Monday to allow a vote on the nomination of Alexis Herman to be Secretary of Labour.

Herman was approved unanimously by the Senate Labour Committee April 10, but Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said last week the full Senate would not vote on her nomination until Clinton clarified his policy on requiring federal construction contracts be performed by union labour.

"It looks absolutely nil," Daschle, of South Dakota, told reporters when asked about the chances of a vote this week. "They (Republicans) are holding her hostage to this federal contract matter. There is no reason to hold up her nomination any longer."

President Clinton Sunday appealed to union members to pressure the Senate to confirm Herman. "I want you to help me get Alexis Herman confirmed as secretary of labour," he told a meeting of some 1,500 members of the United Auto Workers at their annual legislative conference in Washington.

Clinton chose Herman last December as part of his second term cabinet changes, but her nomination was held up for almost three months until she resolved questions about whether she was involved in politics while she was director of the White House Office of Public Liaison.
